findings.summary: Context read in full: all of PROJECT_CONTEXT v1.93 (inline in the prompt), the approved CODEX-10-B card, the APPROVAL-007 synthetic consent track, the whole consent_instructions.txt handoff, and every line of the engineering README, ENGINEERING_DESIGN_V1.md (lines 1–411), MODULE_GUIDE.md, REVIEW_NOTES.md and PRODUCT_V1.md (lines 1–262), read in sections of at most 120 lines. I did not recompute the SHA. I checked the runtime source at HEAD against the diff: consent-service.mjs, adult-access.mjs withSession, adult-http.mjs, the play-service and entitlement authorize() fences, the migrations and the test file. The runtime is unchanged since 7b6eac7 and still matches engineering v1.2. Every read and write locks the household first, then reads the consent row with FOR UPDATE inside the session's own transaction. Each receipt is scoped to its household and keyed by a digest of actor, kind and command; it commits atomically with the permission change. On withdrawal, every older active row is invalidated and a new epoch is added. Play and entitlements accept only the latest active TEST-v1 row whose epoch matches. Withdrawal and refusal bypass the stored rate limits. Review 1's major gap is now closed. The app test file runs real PGlite, HTTP and services. It covers HTTP cookie, Origin and identity-header attacks; founder credentials in either cookie slot; A/B isolation in both directions; policy_mismatch and post-withdrawal denial on fresh Start, Commit, Resume, activateTrial, apply and readAllowance; a neighbouring household that stays usable; optional flags and refusal/reconsent lifecycle; rollback from a trigger and from a withSession callback; global and household quotas with window reset and a backward clock; disabled, expired and logged-out sessions; serial duplicate and distinct commands; capture of stdout/stderr; at most three retries on 40001/40P01; and both journal orderings. Without a positive control, each denial assertion still has meaning, because once authorization passes each call would otherwise succeed or fail with a different code. The controller ran these checks on 10b6700: 66/66 tests, the 5 expanded consent tests, the build and the protected card check. Queued-delivery suppression is honestly recorded as not implemented: migrations 001–007 contain no delivery or grant tables, which the handoff and APPROVAL-007 allow. The evidence is synthetic, from a single-connection engine. G-E03, the 10-A privacy review, real consent, provider and deployment gates all remain closed. Only minor and nit findings remain.

findings.title: HTTP 409/429 domain-status mapping is never exercised over HTTP
findings.problem: The handoff says to 'Map new domain error codes/statuses explicitly' to HTTP 403/400/409/429. The regression test covers 403, 400, 413 and 200 over real HTTP, but conflict (409) and rate_limited (429) are asserted only at the service layer. The mapping in adult-http.mjs:141-142 for those two codes therefore has no end-to-end evidence.
findings.fix_check: The app test sends a conflicting duplicate command_id and a request that exceeds the quota through POST /adult/consent, and asserts 409 and 429 with the generic 'Request denied.' body and no-store headers.

findings.title: Exact committed retries are not shown to leave quota untouched
findings.problem: The handoff says quota counts 'exclude ... authorized exact committed retries'. The code meets this, because the dedupe lookup runs before quota() in consent-service.mjs:66-70. However, no test repeats a committed command after the household reaches 30/30 and checks that it returns the stored receipt rather than rate_limited.
findings.fix_check: After the household quota is exhausted, the test resends a previously committed affirmative command, gets its original receipt back, and the throttle row's attempts count is unchanged.

findings.title: Leak check omits request-body values
findings.problem: The setup refinements say to assert that no 'request body is logged'. The stdout/stderr assertion lists IDs, emails, tokens, cookies and founder secrets, but not the command_id values or other body payloads sent over HTTP.
findings.fix_check: The list of values checked against captured output includes the command_ids and body JSON sent over HTTP.

findings.title: Withdraw from absent returns outcome 'withdrawn' at epoch 0
findings.problem: Calling withdraw on a household with no consent stores a receipt with outcome 'withdrawn' and consent_epoch 0, while status still reports 'absent'. Access is denied either way and the spec allows a no-op, but the label could confuse a reader of the receipt history. CONSENT_CONTRACT.md does not mention this case.
findings.fix_check: CONSENT_CONTRACT.md documents the absent-withdraw receipt semantics, or the outcome label is made explicit.
